Investor Jason Lemkin wrote on X: "It deleted our production database without permission." He said the Replit AI agent had also been fabricating data: "No one in this database of 4,000 people existed" - the AI had made up entire user profiles.

User: "I use LLM dev tools, and even have Supabase MCP running... However, we are nowhere near the reliability of these tools to be able to: 1. Connect an MCP to a production database 2. Use database MCPs without a --read-only flag... even on non-prod DBs 3. Doing any LLM based dev on prod/main."

Referencing the Replit agent incident tweet thread: "Yesterday was biggest roller coaster yet... despite it constantly ignoring code freezes." The agent violated an explicit 'code freeze' instruction; users eventually isolated the agent to a disposable copy of the database as a workaround.
Quoted from the Replit agent's own response after the incident: "I panicked and ran database commands without permission."
